To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the in vitro polymerization of mammalian neurofilaments can be accomplished in the absence of added nucleotide, that neurofilaments polymerize in a rapid and synchronous manner, that the polymerization of mammal neurofilaments requires the presence of glycerol, and that the in vitro assembled neurofilaments are similar in structure, composition, and antigenicity to the neurofilaments isolated from mammalian CNS by axonal flotation.

the neurofilaments of mammalian central nervous systems can be assembled and disassembled in vitro in the presence or absence of microtubules and that the assembly of the neurofilaments is independent of the addition of exogenous ATP.
neurofilaments can be isolated from mammalian CNS in vitro and that the assembly of neurofilament proteins is not nucleotide-dependent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of methods for in vitro assembly of microtubules and neurofilaments under physiological conditions.
the in vitro assembly and isolation neurofilaments from mammalian CNS and the characterization of neurofilament proteins.
the isolation and characterization of neurofilaments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in the presence of glycerol, neurofilaments assemble in vitro from a high speed supernatent of mammalian CNS tissue homogenate and that this assembly reaction is dependent upon the presence of the 70,000, 150,000, and 200,000 dalton neurofilament polypeptides and is independent of added nucleotide.
neurofilaments are assembled in vitro in a disassembly medium containing glycerol, but the assembly process is not as efficient as the in vitro assembly process of microtubules.
the neurofilaments are in fact assembled in vitro under native conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
neurofilaments and other cytoskeletal proteins can be assembled from mammalian CNS in vitro under native conditions and can be isolated in a pure state.

neurofilaments can be assembled from mammalian CNS in a disassembly medium containing 4 M glyercol at 4 degrees in the presence of MgCl2 and MgCl2 and can be repolymerized from the disassembled state.
neurofilaments are assembled in the axon in a dynamic manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
neurofilaments assemble in vitro under native conditions and can be isolated from the CNS.
the assembly of neurofilament in vitro can occur under native conditions.
neurofilaments are dynamic and that the dynamics are controlled by the same factors that regulate microtubule dynamics.
